deals.proximityHighways: Frontage on Bryan Station Road / Route 4 (New Circle Road corridor), a major arterial carrying 35,000+ VPD, with convenient access to I-64 (105,332 VPD). Roughly 3 miles northeast of downtown Lexington; Hamburg Pavilion, War Admiral Place and Sir Barton Place regional retail lie to the east.
deals.retailCotenants: Shadow-anchored by a Kroger on the adjacent NAP parcel (1M+ annual visits). Competing/complementary centers in the trade area include North Park Marketplace, Meadowthorpe Center, Eastland Shopping Center and the Hamburg Pavilion / War Admiral Place / Sir Barton Place node.
deals.shadowAnchors: Kroger — occupies the adjacent NAP parcel (not owned, not part of the offering) and contributes $2,472/yr toward shared parking-lot utilities, growing 3% annually. Generates 1M+ annual visits and is the center's principal traffic driver. Fifth Third Bank and Healthfirst occupy outparcels (suites BANK and OUT2) that pay no base rent to ownership and contribute only their share of CAM (excluding fire sprinkler, roof repairs and sprinkler inspections) under agreements running to 12/31/2045.

keyAssumptions: ROSTER BASIS: the roster is CBRE's IN-PLACE PRO-FORMA for calendar year 2027 (page 9), not a raw as-of-today rent roll. Annual rents and PSF are the CY2027 contractual amounts, which is what the $615,795 in-place NOI, the $244,838 recovery line and the $888,433 EGR all tie to. CBRE's own note: in-place NOI uses contractual rents Jan-27 to Dec-27 with no general vacancy loss, excludes vacant lease-up revenue and near-term-expiry downtime, but DOES include future rent increases for existing tenants.

The roster ties out four ways against the OM's printed totals: (a) 51,275 SF occupied + 3,002 SF vacant = 54,277 SF GLA; (b) 51,275 / 54,277 = 94.5% = the stated occupancy; (c) base rents sum to $643,595 = the OM's Total Scheduled Base Rent; (d) $888,433 EGR - $272,638 OpEx = $615,795 NOI. Tenant recoveries sum to $244,839 vs the $244,838 printed (rounding).

WALT of 3.64 years is the OM-stated figure and reproduces exactly when computed SF-weighted from the roster's expiries as of 01/01/2027 (the analysis commencement date) — an independent confirmation that the roster is complete.
NO PRICE AND NO CAP RATE are quoted — this is an unpriced marketing package. Value must be underwritten off the $615,795 in-place NOI.

TAXES ARE NOT REASSESSED. CBRE's $88,475 CY2027 real-estate tax line equals the 2026 budget grown forward; the OM states expressly that it is the investor's responsibility to reassess. Fayette County, KY is an annual-assessment jurisdiction, so a sale will very likely reset the assessment to the purchase price — model the step-up before bidding.

Expenses are CBRE's model of the 2026 budget, with non-recoverable ownership-specific expenses stripped out and replaced by a $0.05/SF assumption. Reimbursements toward amortized deferred capital projects are modeled BELOW the NOI line, so the recovery figure here excludes them.

Three roster rows (Fifth Third suite BANK, Healthfirst suite OUT2, Kroger suite NAP) carry no SF and no base rent — they contribute CAM only, on agreements dated to 12/31/2045. They are carried as NAP so they do not distort GLA, occupancy or rent-PSF math; their $33,663 of combined CAM contribution IS inside the center's $244,838 recovery line.

The OM does not print a year built, a renovation year, or the individual lease rent-step schedules, renewal-option terms, or co-tenancy/kickout clauses. Those are all left null rather than estimated — pull the rent roll and leases in diligence.
No OM date is printed on the Bryan Station package (the sister Project Evergreen books are stamped July-August 2026), so omDate is left null.

redFlags.description: Cato is the center's clear problem tenant: $79 PSF of sales against a 21.32% occupancy cost (OM-stated) on 6,080 SF, expiring 01/31/2028 with NO remaining renewal options. The OM presents Cato among its below-market mark-to-market opportunities; the sales data says the opposite — this is a renewal/vacancy risk on 11% of GLA, not upside.

39% of GLA (Planet Fitness, 20,955 SF) rolls in a single year, 08/03/2032, and it is the only in-line anchor. There is no disclosed renewal option and no co-tenancy protection. A Planet Fitness non-renewal is the single largest swing factor in the hold.

The real anchor is NOT owned. Kroger sits on the NAP parcel and drives the 1M+ annual visits the whole investment thesis rests on, but ownership has no lease, no term, and no go-dark protection over it — only a $2,472/yr shared-utility contribution. A Kroger closure or relocation would hit in-line rents with nothing to offset it.

Near-term rollover is heavy and largely unprotected: KORT Physical Therapy (5,000 SF, 11/30/2027), New York Fashions (3,060 SF, 12/31/2027), Cato (6,080 SF, 01/31/2028), Nails Pro (900 SF, 03/31/2028) and China King (1,050 SF, 05/31/2028) — 16,090 SF / 29.6% of GLA — expire within roughly 18 months of the CY2027 analysis start, and the OM says four of them have no remaining options. CBRE's in-place NOI assumes they simply stay at current rents, so the $615,795 carries no downtime or re-leasing cost for any of it.

Taxes are NOT reassessed in the pro-forma. Kentucky assesses at fair cash value annually; a purchase will very likely reset the assessment, and the $88,475 modeled tax line is 14% of NOI — a meaningful post-close step-up risk the pro-forma does not carry.

Cato's 5% NON-CUMULATIVE cap on CAM, taxes AND insurance caps recovery growth on 11% of GLA. Because it covers taxes as well as CAM, it also blunts the recovery of any post-sale tax reassessment on that suite.
Sales data is disclosed for only two of the ten in-line tenants (Shoe Station and Cato). Occupancy cost and tenant health are unknown for the rest of the roster, including Planet Fitness.

upsideItems.detail: Lease-up of the 3,002 SF vacancy (suite 140) — CBRE models absorption at 1/1/2028 at $15.00/SF shop market rent; the OM cites $51,000+ of incremental annual base rent plus NNN reimbursements.

upsideItems.item: Mark to market on Planet Fitness and Pizza Hut
upsideItems.detail: Mark-to-market on genuinely below-market leases: Pizza Hut at $10.20/SF and Planet Fitness at $8.41/SF sit far below the $14.34/SF 2027 weighted-average market rent CBRE models for the center. Shoe Station at $14.50/SF on $168 PSF of sales (11.13% occupancy cost) also has room. Note that Cato and China King, which the OM groups into this same upside bucket, do NOT belong there — Cato's sales are too weak and China King is already the highest-rented suite in the center.
In-place rent of $12.55/SF vs CBRE's $14.34/SF 2027 market rent is a ~14% aggregate mark-to-market gap; the modeled 10-year NOI CAGR is 4.08%, reaching $918,228 by CY2037.

upsideItems.item: Contractual NOI growth with no leasing required
upsideItems.detail: Contractual growth without any leasing: the OM's own in-place NOI already steps from $615,795 (CY2027) to $691,955 (CY2028) and $737,422 (CY2029), driven by contractual increases plus the modeled lease-up.

upsideItems.item: Proven tenant stickiness on the 2027-28 roll
upsideItems.detail: Tenant stickiness — the OM reports ~19,420 SF of lease extensions executed over the past three years and 67% of the roster in place for 10+ years, which supports renewal probability on the heavy 2027-2028 roll.

Trade-area income growth: 3-mile average household income of $97,726 projected to grow 16.10% over five years, with a 104,740 daytime population and $379,812 average home values — a supportive backdrop for pushing shop rents.

deals.notes: Bryan Station is a 54,277 SF neighborhood shopping center on Bryan Station Road in northeast Lexington, Kentucky, offered unpriced by CBRE as part of the Project Evergreen portfolio. The asset's traffic thesis rests on a Kroger that generates over 1 million annual visits — but that Kroger sits on the adjacent NAP parcel and is NOT part of the offering, so ownership carries none of the lease control that normally underpins a grocery-anchored center. The owned rent roll is 94.5% leased at a $12.55/SF weighted-average base rent against CBRE's $14.34/SF modeled market rent, producing $615,795 of CY2027 in-place NOI on $888,433 of effective gross revenue and $272,638 of operating expenses. Planet Fitness is the only in-line anchor at 20,955 SF (38.6% of GLA) and pays just $8.41/SF through August 2032, which is real mark-to-market depth but also concentrates 39% of the center's area in one uncontracted 2032 expiry. The near-term picture is busier than the headline suggests: KORT Physical Therapy, New York Fashions, Cato, Nails Pro and China King — 16,090 SF, 29.6% of GLA — all expire between November 2027 and May 2028, and CBRE's in-place NOI simply assumes they hold over at current rents with no downtime or re-leasing cost. Cato is the tenant to underwrite hardest: $79 PSF of sales against a 21.32% occupancy cost on 6,080 SF expiring January 2028 with no options is a vacancy risk, notwithstanding the OM's framing of it as below-market upside. The investment case is a 4.08% modeled 10-year NOI CAGR from lease-up of the single 3,002 SF vacancy plus mark-to-market on Planet Fitness and Pizza Hut, into a trade area with a $97,726 3-mile average household income growing 16% over five years. The top risk is structural rather than operational — an un-owned grocery anchor and a single 39%-of-GLA fitness tenant carry the traffic and the income, and neither is protected by anything in the deal.
